newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish recovery extends into 1997 - Bank of Spain.
newsitem.headline: Spanish recovery extends into 1997 - Bank of Spain.

text.p: In the first few months of 1997, the Spanish economy confirmed the recovery trend seen in 1996, the Bank of Spain said in a monthly report released on Monday.
"The gradual recovery of economic activity of 1996 continued in the first months of 1997, backed by a more dynamic trend in domestic demand," the central bank said.
"Private consumption indicators streghtened their recovery, while investment in capital goods remained high and the shortfall in the building sector slowed down," the report said.
Exports remained high, while imports increased at a accelerating pace.

The central bank underlined the strength of new job formation at the beginning of 1997 and added that while inflation had moderated to 1.7 percent, salaries were rising at "levels of above three percent."
